   129→def _show_post_scan_analysis(diff: dict, state: dict, lang) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:
   130→    """Print warnings, narrative headline, and top action. Returns (warnings, narrative)."""
   131→    warnings = []
   132→    if diff["reopened"] > 5:
   133→        warnings.append(f"{diff['reopened']} findings reopened — was a previous fix reverted? Check: git log --oneline -5")
   134→    if diff["new"] > 10 and diff["auto_resolved"] < 3:
   135→        warnings.append(f"{diff['new']} new findings with few resolutions — likely cascading from recent fixes. Run fixers again.")
   136→    chronic = diff.get("chronic_reopeners", [])
   137→    n = len(chronic) if isinstance(chronic, list) else chronic
   138→    if n > 0:
   139→        warnings.append(f"⟳ {n} chronic reopener{'s' if n != 1 else ''} (reopened 2+ times). "
   140→                        f"These keep bouncing — fix properly or wontfix. "
   141→                        f"Run: `desloppify show --chronic` to see them.")
   142→
   143→    if warnings:
   144→        for w in warnings:
   145→            print(colorize(f"  {w}", "yellow"))
   146→        print()
   147→
   148→    # Computed narrative: headline + top action as terminal suggestion
   149→    print(colorize("\n  INSTRUCTIONS FOR AGENTS: follow the strategy and recommendations below.", "yellow"))
   150→    from ..narrative import compute_narrative
   151→    lang_name = lang.name if lang else None
   152→    narrative = compute_narrative(state, diff=diff, lang=lang_name, command="scan")
   153→
   154→    # Show strategy hint or top action as the terminal suggestion
   155→    strategy = narrative.get("strategy") or {}
   156→    hint = strategy.get("hint")
   157→    fixer_rec = (strategy.get("fixer_leverage") or {}).get("recommendation")
   158→    actions = narrative.get("actions", [])
   159→
   160→    if hint and (strategy.get("can_parallelize") or fixer_rec == "strong"):
   161→        print(colorize(f"  Strategy: {hint}", "cyan"))
   162→        if actions:
   163→            print(colorize(f"  Start with: `{actions[0]['command']}`", "dim"))
   164→        print()
   165→    elif actions:
   166→        top = actions[0]
   167→        print(colorize(f"  Suggested next: `{top['command']}` — {top['description']}", "cyan"))
   168→        print()
   169→
   170→    if narrative.get("headline"):
   171→        print(colorize(f"  → {narrative['headline']}", "cyan"))
   172→        print()
   173→
   174→    # Review findings nudge
   175→    from ..state import path_scoped_findings
   176→    open_review = [f for f in path_scoped_findings(
   177→        state.get("findings", {}), state.get("scan_path")).values()
   178→                   if f["status"] == "open" and f.get("detector") == "review"]
   179→    if open_review:
   180→        s = "s" if len(open_review) != 1 else ""
   181→        print(colorize(f"  Review: {len(open_review)} finding{s} pending \u2014 `desloppify issues`", "cyan"))
   182→        print()
   183→
   184→    # Auto-queue: nudge subjective review for high-complexity unreviewed files
   185→    review_cache = state.get("review_cache", {}).get("files", {})
   186→    scoped = path_scoped_findings(state.get("findings", {}), state.get("scan_path"))
   187→    complex_unreviewed = set()
   188→    for f in scoped.values():
   189→        if (f.get("detector") in ("structural", "smells")
   190→                and f.get("status") == "wontfix"
   191→                and f.get("file") not in review_cache):
   192→            complex_unreviewed.add(f.get("file"))
   193→    if len(complex_unreviewed) >= 3:
   194→        print(colorize(f"  {len(complex_unreviewed)} complex files have never been reviewed — "
   195→                        f"`desloppify review --prepare` would provide actionable refactoring guidance", "dim"))
   196→        print()
   197→
   198→    return warnings, narrative
   199→

   201→def cmd_scan(args):
   202→    """Run all detectors, update persistent state, show diff."""
   203→    from ..state import load_state, save_state, merge_scan
   204→    from ..plan import generate_findings
   205→
   206→    sp = _state_path(args)
   207→    state = load_state(sp)
   208→    path = Path(args.path)
   209→    include_slow = not getattr(args, "skip_slow", False)
   210→
   211→    # Persist --exclude in config so subsequent commands reuse it
   212→    from ..config import save_config
   213→    config = args._config
   214→    exclude = getattr(args, "exclude", None)
   215→    if exclude:
   216→        config["exclude"] = list(exclude)
   217→        save_config(config)
   218→
   219→    # Resolve language config
   220→    from ._helpers import _resolve_lang
   221→    lang = _resolve_lang(args)
   222→    lang_label = f" ({lang.name})" if lang else ""
   223→
   224→    # Load zone overrides from config
   225→    zone_overrides = config.get("zone_overrides") or None
   226→
   227→    # Populate review cache and max age for review_coverage detector
   228→    if lang:
   229→        lang._review_cache = state.get("review_cache", {}).get("files", {})
   230→        lang._review_max_age_days = config.get("review_max_age_days", 30)
   231→        # Apply config-level threshold overrides
   232→        override_threshold = config.get("large_files_threshold", 0)
   233→        if override_threshold > 0:
   234→            lang.large_threshold = override_threshold
   235→        props_threshold = config.get("props_threshold", 0)
   236→        if props_threshold > 0:
   237→            lang._props_threshold = props_threshold
   238→
   239→    print(colorize(f"\nDesloppify Scan{lang_label}\n", "bold"))
   240→    from ..utils import enable_file_cache, disable_file_cache
   241→    enable_file_cache()
   242→    try:
   243→        findings, potentials = generate_findings(path, include_slow=include_slow, lang=lang,
   244→                                                  zone_overrides=zone_overrides)
   245→    finally:
   246→        disable_file_cache()
   247→
   248→    codebase_metrics = _collect_codebase_metrics(lang, path)
   249→
   250→    from ..utils import rel, get_exclusions, PROJECT_ROOT
   251→
   252→    # Audit excluded directories for staleness (Issue #11)
   253→    extra_ex = get_exclusions()
   254→    if extra_ex and lang and lang.file_finder:
   255→        scanned_files = lang.file_finder(path)
   256→        stale = _audit_excluded_dirs(extra_ex, scanned_files, PROJECT_ROOT)
   257→        if stale:
   258→            findings.extend(stale)
   259→            for sf in stale:
   260→                print(colorize(f"  ℹ {sf['summary']}", "dim"))
   261→    scan_path_rel = rel(str(path))
   262→
   263→    prev_scan_path = state.get("scan_path")
   264→    path_changed = prev_scan_path is not None and prev_scan_path != scan_path_rel
   265→    prev_score = state.get("score", 0) if not path_changed else 0
   266→    prev_strict = state.get("strict_score", 0) if not path_changed else 0
   267→    prev_obj = state.get("objective_score") if not path_changed else None
   268→    prev_obj_strict = state.get("objective_strict") if not path_changed else None
   269→    # Persist zone distribution before save so narrative can access it
   270→    if lang and lang._zone_map is not None:
   271→        state["zone_distribution"] = lang._zone_map.counts()
   272→
   273→    prev_dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {}) if not path_changed else {}
   274→    diff = merge_scan(state, findings,
   275→                      lang=lang.name if lang else None,
   276→                      scan_path=scan_path_rel,
   277→                      force_resolve=getattr(args, "force_resolve", False),
   278→                      exclude=get_exclusions(),
   279→                      potentials=potentials,
   280→                      codebase_metrics=codebase_metrics,
   281→                      include_slow=include_slow,
   282→                      ignore=config.get("ignore", []))
   283→
   284→    # Expire stale holistic review findings
   285→    from ..issues import expire_stale_holistic
   286→    holistic_max_age = config.get("holistic_max_age_days", 30)
   287→    expire_stale_holistic(state, holistic_max_age)
   288→
   289→    save_state(state, sp)
   290→
   291→    print(colorize("\n  AGENT: PLEASE READ the strategy and recommendations below the score.", "yellow"))
   292→    print(colorize("  They are CUSTOM COACHING tailored to this codebase. Follow them.", "yellow"))
   293→    print(colorize("  Scan complete", "bold"))
   294→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 50, "dim"))
   295→
   296→    _show_diff_summary(diff)
   297→    _show_score_delta(state, prev_score, prev_strict, prev_obj, prev_obj_strict)
   298→    if not include_slow:
   299→        print(colorize("  * Fast scan — slow phases (duplicates) skipped", "yellow"))
   300→    _show_detector_progress(state)
   301→
   302→    # Dimension deltas and low-dimension hints
   303→    new_dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {})
   304→    if new_dim_scores and prev_dim_scores:
   305→        _show_dimension_deltas(prev_dim_scores, new_dim_scores)
   306→    if new_dim_scores:
   307→        _show_low_dimension_hints(new_dim_scores)
   308→
   309→    _show_score_integrity(state, diff)
   310→
   311→    zone_distribution = state.get("zone_distribution")
   312→
   313→    warnings, narrative = _show_post_scan_analysis(diff, state, lang)
   314→
   315→    # Persist reminder history (computed by narrative, not mutated)
   316→    if narrative and "reminder_history" in narrative:
   317→        state["reminder_history"] = narrative["reminder_history"]
   318→        save_state(state, sp)
   319→
   320→    from ..config import config_for_query
   321→    _write_query({"command": "scan", "score": state["score"],
   322→                  "strict_score": state.get("strict_score", 0),
   323→                  "prev_score": prev_score, "diff": diff, "stats": state["stats"],
   324→                  "warnings": warnings,
   325→                  "objective_score": state.get("objective_score"),
   326→                  "objective_strict": state.get("objective_strict"),
   327→                  "dimension_scores": state.get("dimension_scores"),
   328→                  "potentials": state.get("potentials"),
   329→                  "zone_distribution": zone_distribution,
   330→                  "narrative": narrative,
   331→                  "config": config_for_query(config)})
   332→
   333→    # Generate scorecard badge
   334→    badge_path = None
   335→    try:
   336→        from ..output.scorecard import generate_scorecard, get_badge_config
   337→        badge_path, disabled = get_badge_config(args, config)
   338→        if not disabled and badge_path:
   339→            generate_scorecard(state, badge_path)
   340→            rel_path = badge_path.name if badge_path.parent == PROJECT_ROOT else str(badge_path)
   341→            # Check if README already references the scorecard
   342→            readme_has_badge = False
   343→            for readme_name in ("README.md", "readme.md", "README.MD"):
   344→                readme_path = PROJECT_ROOT / readme_name
   345→                if readme_path.exists():
   346→                    try:
   347→                        if rel_path in readme_path.read_text():
   348→                            readme_has_badge = True
   349→                    except OSError:
   350→                        pass
   351→                    break
   352→            if readme_has_badge:
   353→                print(colorize(f"  Scorecard → {rel_path}  (disable: --no-badge | move: --badge-path <path>)", "dim"))
   354→            else:
   355→                print(colorize(f"  Scorecard → {rel_path}", "dim"))
   356→                print(colorize(f"  💡 Ask the user if they'd like to add it to their README with:", "dim"))
   357→                print(colorize(f'     <img src="{rel_path}" width="100%">', "dim"))
   358→                print(colorize(f"     (disable: --no-badge | move: --badge-path <path>)", "dim"))
   359→        else:
   360→            badge_path = None
   361→    except (ImportError, OSError):
   362→        badge_path = None  # Pillow not installed or write failed — skip silently
   363→
   364→    _print_llm_summary(state, badge_path, narrative, diff)

   367→def _show_score_integrity(state: dict, diff: dict):
   368→    """Show Score Integrity section — surfaces wontfix debt and ignored findings."""
   369→    stats = state.get("stats", {})
   370→    wontfix = stats.get("wontfix", 0)
   371→    ignored = diff.get("ignored", 0)
   372→    ignore_patterns = diff.get("ignore_patterns", 0)
   373→
   374→    if wontfix <= 5 and ignored <= 0:
   375→        return
   376→
   377→    obj = state.get("objective_score")
   378→    obj_strict = state.get("objective_strict")
   379→    strict_gap = round(obj - obj_strict, 1) if obj is not None and obj_strict is not None else 0
   380→
   381→    # Wontfix % of actionable findings (open + wontfix + fixed + auto_resolved + false_positive)
   382→    actionable = stats.get("open", 0) + wontfix + stats.get("fixed", 0) + stats.get("auto_resolved", 0) + stats.get("false_positive", 0)
   383→    wontfix_pct = round(wontfix / actionable * 100) if actionable else 0
   384→
   385→    print(colorize("  " + "\u2504" * 2 + " Score Integrity " + "\u2504" * 37, "dim"))
   386→
   387→    if wontfix > 5:
   388→        if wontfix_pct > 50:
   389→            style = "red"
   390→            msg = f"  \u274c {wontfix} wontfix ({wontfix_pct}%) \u2014 over half of findings swept under rug. Strict gap: {strict_gap} pts"
   391→        elif wontfix_pct > 25:
   392→            style = "yellow"
   393→            msg = f"  \u26a0 {wontfix} wontfix ({wontfix_pct}%) \u2014 review whether past wontfix decisions still hold"
   394→        elif wontfix_pct > 10:
   395→            style = "yellow"
   396→            msg = f"  \u26a0 {wontfix} wontfix findings ({wontfix_pct}%) \u2014 strict {strict_gap} pts below lenient"
   397→        else:
   398→            style = "dim"
   399→            msg = f"  {wontfix} wontfix \u2014 strict gap: {strict_gap} pts"
   400→        print(colorize(msg, style))
   401→
   402→        # Show top 2 dimensions with biggest strict gap
   403→        dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {})
   404→        if dim_scores:
   405→            gaps = []
   406→            for name, data in dim_scores.items():
   407→                score = data.get("score", 100)
   408→                strict = data.get("strict", score)
   409→                gap = round(score - strict, 1)
   410→                if gap > 0:
   411→                    gaps.append((name, gap))
   412→            gaps.sort(key=lambda x: -x[1])
   413→            if gaps:
   414→                top = gaps[:2]
   415→                gap_str = ", ".join(f"{n} (\u2212{g} pts)" for n, g in top)
   416→                print(colorize(f"    Biggest gaps: {gap_str}", "dim"))
   417→
   418→    if ignored > 0:
   419→        if ignore_patterns > 5 or ignored > 100:
   420→            style = "red"
   421→        else:
   422→            style = "yellow"
   423→        print(colorize(f"  \u26a0 {ignore_patterns} ignore pattern{'s' if ignore_patterns != 1 else ''} "
   424→                        f"suppressed {ignored} finding{'s' if ignored != 1 else ''} this scan", style))
   425→        print(colorize(f"    Ignored findings are invisible to scoring", "dim"))
   426→
   427→    print(colorize("  " + "\u2504" * 55, "dim"))
   428→    print()
   429→

   431→def _print_llm_summary(state: dict, badge_path: Path | None,
   432→                        narrative: dict | None = None,
   433→                        diff: dict | None = None):
   434→    """Print a structured summary for LLM consumption.
   435→
   436→    The LLM reads terminal output after running scans. This gives it
   437→    clear instructions on how to present the results to the end user.
   438→    Only shown when running inside an agent (CLAUDE_CODE or DESLOPPIFY_AGENT env).
   439→    """
   440→    import os
   441→    if not (os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE") or os.environ.get("DESLOPPIFY_AGENT")):
   442→        return
   443→
   444→    dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {})
   445→    obj_score = state.get("objective_score")
   446→    obj_strict = state.get("objective_strict")
   447→    if obj_score is None and not dim_scores:
   448→        return
   449→
   450→    print("─" * 60)
   451→    print("INSTRUCTIONS FOR LLM")
   452→    print("IMPORTANT: ALWAYS present ALL scores to the user after a scan.")
   453→    print("Show overall health (lenient + strict), ALL dimension scores,")
   454→    print("AND all subjective dimension scores in a markdown table.")
   455→    print("The goal is to maximize strict scores. Never skip the scores.\n")
   456→
   457→    print(f"Overall health: {obj_score:.1f}/100")
   458→    if obj_strict is not None:
   459→        print(f"Strict health:  {obj_strict:.1f}/100")
   460→    print()
   461→
   462→    # Build dimension table — separate mechanical from subjective
   463→    from ..scoring import DIMENSIONS
   464→    static_names = {d.name for d in DIMENSIONS}
   465→    mechanical = [(name, data) for name, data in dim_scores.items()
   466→                  if name in static_names and data.get("checks", 0) > 0]
   467→    subjective = [(name, data) for name, data in dim_scores.items()
   468→                  if name not in static_names and data.get("checks", 0) > 0]
   469→
   470→    if mechanical or subjective:
   471→        from ..registry import dimension_action_type
   472→        print("| Dimension | Health | Strict | Issues | Tier | Action |")
   473→        print("|-----------|--------|--------|--------|------|--------|")
   474→        for name, data in sorted(mechanical, key=lambda x: x[0]):
   475→            score = data.get("score", 100)
   476→            strict = data.get("strict", score)
   477→            issues = data.get("issues", 0)
   478→            tier = data.get("tier", "")
   479→            action = dimension_action_type(name)
   480→            print(f"| {name} | {score:.1f}% | {strict:.1f}% | {issues} | T{tier} | {action} |")
   481→        if subjective:
   482→            print("| **Subjective Dimensions** | | | | | |")
   483→            for name, data in sorted(subjective, key=lambda x: x[0]):
   484→                score = data.get("score", 100)
   485→                strict = data.get("strict", score)
   486→                issues = data.get("issues", 0)
   487→                tier = data.get("tier", "")
   488→                print(f"| {name} | {score:.1f}% | {strict:.1f}% | {issues} | T{tier} | review |")
   489→        print()
   490→
   491→    stats = state.get("stats", {})
   492→    if stats:
   493→        wontfix = stats.get("wontfix", 0)
   494→        ignored = diff.get("ignored", 0) if diff else 0
   495→        ignore_pats = diff.get("ignore_patterns", 0) if diff else 0
   496→        strict_gap = round((obj_score or 0) - (obj_strict or 0), 1) if obj_score and obj_strict else 0
   497→        print(f"Total findings: {stats.get('total', 0)} | "
   498→              f"Open: {stats.get('open', 0)} | "
   499→              f"Fixed: {stats.get('fixed', 0)} | "
   500→              f"Wontfix: {wontfix}")
   501→        if wontfix or ignored:
   502→            print(f"Ignored: {ignored} (by {ignore_pats} patterns) | Strict gap: {strict_gap} pts")
   503→            print("Focus on strict score \u2014 wontfix and ignore inflate the lenient score.")
   504→        print()
   505→
   506→    # Workflow guide — teach agents the full cycle
   507→    print("## Workflow Guide\n")
   508→    print("1. **Review findings first** (if any): `desloppify issues` — high-value subjective findings")
   509→    print("2. **Run auto-fixers** (if available): `desloppify fix <fixer> --dry-run` to preview, then apply")
   510→    print("3. **Manual fixes**: `desloppify next` — highest-priority item. Fix it, then:")
   511→    print('   `desloppify resolve fixed "<id>" --note "<what you did>"`')
   512→    print("4. **Rescan**: `desloppify scan --path <path>` — verify improvements, catch cascading effects")
   513→    print("5. **Check progress**: `desloppify status` — dimension scores dashboard\n")
   514→    print("### Decision Guide")
   515→    print("- **Tackle**: T1/T2 (high impact), auto-fixable, security findings")
   516→    print("- **Consider skipping**: T4 low-confidence, test/config zone findings (lower impact)")
   517→    print("- **Wontfix**: Intentional patterns, false positives →")
   518→    print('  `desloppify resolve wontfix "<id>" --note "<why>"`')
   519→    print("- **Batch wontfix**: Multiple intentional patterns →")
   520→    print('  `desloppify resolve wontfix "<detector>::*::<category>" --note "<why>"`\n')
   521→    print("### Understanding Dimensions")
   522→    print("- **Mechanical** (File health, Code quality, etc.): Fix code → rescan")
   523→    print("- **Subjective** (Naming Quality, Logic Clarity, etc.): Address review findings → re-review")
   524→    print("- **Health vs Strict**: Health ignores wontfix; Strict penalizes it. Focus on Strict.\n")
   525→
   526→    # Current narrative status
   527→    if narrative:
   528→        headline = narrative.get("headline", "")
   529→        strategy = narrative.get("strategy") or {}
   530→        actions = narrative.get("actions", [])
   531→        if headline:
   532→            print(f"Current status: {headline}")
   533→        hint = strategy.get("hint", "")
   534→        if hint:
   535→            print(f"Strategy: {hint}")
   536→        if actions:
   537→            top = actions[0]
   538→            print(f"Top action: `{top['command']}` — {top['description']}")
   539→        print()
   540→
   541→    if badge_path and badge_path.exists():
   542→        from ..utils import PROJECT_ROOT
   543→        rel_path = badge_path.name if badge_path.parent == PROJECT_ROOT else str(badge_path)
   544→        print(f"A scorecard image was saved to `{rel_path}`.")
   545→        print("Let the user know they can view it, and suggest adding it")
   546→        print(f'to their README: `<img src="{rel_path}" width="100%">`')
   547→    print("─" * 60)
   548→
   549→
   550→def _show_detector_progress(state: dict):
   551→    """Show per-detector progress bars — the heartbeat of a scan."""
   552→    from ..state import path_scoped_findings
   553→    findings = path_scoped_findings(state["findings"], state.get("scan_path"))
   554→    if not findings:
   555→        return
   556→
   557→    from ..narrative import STRUCTURAL_MERGE
   558→    by_det: dict[str, dict] = {}
   559→    for f in findings.values():
   560→        det = f.get("detector", "unknown")
   561→        if det in STRUCTURAL_MERGE:
   562→            det = "structural"
   563→        if det not in by_det:
   564→            by_det[det] = {"open": 0, "total": 0}
   565→        by_det[det]["total"] += 1
   566→        if f["status"] == "open":
   567→            by_det[det]["open"] += 1
   568→
   569→    from ..registry import display_order, DETECTORS
   570→    DET_ORDER = [DETECTORS[d].display for d in display_order() if d in DETECTORS]
   571→    order_map = {d: i for i, d in enumerate(DET_ORDER)}
   572→    sorted_dets = sorted(by_det.items(), key=lambda x: order_map.get(x[0], 99))
   573→
   574→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 50, "dim"))
   575→    bar_len = 15
   576→    for det, ds in sorted_dets:
   577→        total = ds["total"]
   578→        open_count = ds["open"]
   579→        addressed = total - open_count
   580→        pct = round(addressed / total * 100) if total else 100
   581→
   582→        filled = round(pct / 100 * bar_len)
   583→        if pct == 100:
   584→            bar = colorize("█" * bar_len, "green")
   585→        elif open_count <= 2:
   586→            bar = colorize("█" * filled, "green") + colorize("░" * (bar_len - filled), "dim")
   587→        else:
   588→            bar = colorize("█" * filled, "yellow") + colorize("░" * (bar_len - filled), "dim")
   589→
   590→        det_label = det.replace("_", " ").ljust(18)
   591→        if open_count > 0:
   592→            open_str = colorize(f"{open_count:3d} open", "yellow")
   593→        else:
   594→            open_str = colorize("  ✓", "green")
   595→
   596→        print(f"  {det_label} {bar} {pct:3d}%  {open_str}  {colorize(f'/ {total}', 'dim')}")
   597→
   598→    print()

   601→def _show_dimension_deltas(prev: dict, current: dict):
   602→    """Show which dimensions changed between scans (health and strict)."""
   603→    from ..scoring import DIMENSIONS
   604→    moved = []
   605→    for dim in DIMENSIONS:
   606→        p = prev.get(dim.name, {})
   607→        n = current.get(dim.name, {})
   608→        if not p or not n:
   609→            continue
   610→        old_score = p.get("score", 100)
   611→        new_score = n.get("score", 100)
   612→        old_strict = p.get("strict", old_score)
   613→        new_strict = n.get("strict", new_score)
   614→        delta = new_score - old_score
   615→        strict_delta = new_strict - old_strict
   616→        if abs(delta) >= 0.1 or abs(strict_delta) >= 0.1:
   617→            moved.append((dim.name, old_score, new_score, delta, old_strict, new_strict, strict_delta))
   618→
   619→    if not moved:
   620→        return
   621→
   622→    print(colorize("  Moved:", "dim"))
   623→    for name, old, new, delta, old_s, new_s, s_delta in sorted(moved, key=lambda x: x[3]):
   624→        sign = "+" if delta > 0 else ""
   625→        color = "green" if delta > 0 else "red"
   626→        strict_str = ""
   627→        if abs(s_delta) >= 0.1:
   628→            s_sign = "+" if s_delta > 0 else ""
   629→            strict_str = colorize(f"  strict: {old_s:.1f}→{new_s:.1f}% ({s_sign}{s_delta:.1f}%)", "dim")
   630→        print(colorize(f"    {name:<22} {old:.1f}% → {new:.1f}%  ({sign}{delta:.1f}%)", color) + strict_str)
   631→    print()
   632→
   633→
   634→def _show_low_dimension_hints(dim_scores: dict):
   635→    """Show actionable hints for dimensions below 50%."""
   636→    from ..scoring import DIMENSIONS
   637→    static_names = {d.name for d in DIMENSIONS}
   638→
   639→    _MECHANICAL_HINTS = {
   640→        "File health": "run `desloppify show structural` — split large files",
   641→        "Code quality": "run `desloppify show smells` — fix code smells",
   642→        "Duplication": "run `desloppify show dupes` — deduplicate functions",
   643→        "Test health": "add tests for uncovered files: `desloppify show test_coverage`",
   644→        "Security": "run `desloppify show security` — fix security issues",
   645→    }
   646→
   647→    low = []
   648→    for name, data in dim_scores.items():
   649→        strict = data.get("strict", data.get("score", 100))
   650→        if strict < 50:
   651→            if name in static_names:
   652→                hint = _MECHANICAL_HINTS.get(name, "run `desloppify show` for details")
   653→            else:
   654→                hint = "run `desloppify review --prepare` to assess"
   655→            low.append((name, strict, hint))
   656→
   657→    if not low:
   658→        return
   659→
   660→    low.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
   661→    print(colorize("  Needs attention:", "yellow"))
   662→    for name, score, hint in low:
   663→        print(colorize(f"    {name} ({score:.0f}%) — {hint}", "yellow"))
   664→    print()

    12→def _dedup(replacements: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:

    14→    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    15→    result = []

   136→def _safe_write(filepath: str | Path, content: str) -> None:
   137→    """Atomic write: write to temp file then rename."""
   138→    p = Path(filepath)
   139→    tmp = p.with_suffix(p.suffix + ".tmp")
   140→    try:
   141→        tmp.write_text(content)
   142→        os.replace(str(tmp), str(p))
   143→    except BaseException:
   144→        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
   145→        raise

   148→def _apply_changes(
   149→    source_abs: str, dest_abs: str,
   150→    importer_changes: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]],

   152→) -> None:
   153→    """Move the file and apply all import replacements.
   154→
   155→    Uses a two-phase approach: compute all new content first, then write.
   156→    On error, attempts to roll back by restoring original file contents.
   157→    """
   158→    # Phase 1: Read all files and compute new contents (no writes yet)
   159→    new_contents: dict[str, str] = {}
   160→    if self_changes:
   161→        content = Path(source_abs).read_text()
   162→        for old_str, new_str in self_changes:
   163→            content = content.replace(old_str, new_str)

   170→        new_contents[filepath] = content
   171→
   172→    # Phase 2: Move file and write all changes

   174→    written_files: dict[str, str] = {}  # filepath -> original content (for rollback)

   177→
   178→        # Write self-import changes to moved file
   179→        if dest_abs in new_contents:

   182→
   183→        # Write importer changes

   187→                _safe_write(filepath, new_contents[filepath])

   189→    except Exception as ex:

   192→        # Restore any files we already wrote

   198→        # Move the file back if it was moved
   199→        if Path(dest_abs).exists() and not Path(source_abs).exists():

   202→            except OSError:
   203→                print(colorize(f"  WARNING: Could not move file back to {rel(source_abs)}", "red"),
   204→                      file=sys.stderr)
   205→        raise

   451→        for fp, original in written_files.items():

   325→        for reason, count in sorted(skip_reasons.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):

   332→    checklist += ["Run `desloppify scan` to update state. Did score improve as expected?",
   333→                  "Are there cascading effects? (e.g., removing vars may orphan imports)",

    44→    for f in sorted(files, key=lambda f: rel(f)):
    45→        zone = zone_map.get(f)
    46→        by_zone.setdefault(zone.value, []).append(f)

    51→    for zone_val in ["production", "test", "config", "generated", "script", "vendor"]:

    53→        if not zone_files:
    54→            continue
    55→        print(colorize(f"  {zone_val} ({len(zone_files)} files)", "bold"))
    56→        for f in zone_files:
    57→            rp = rel(f)

    59→            suffix = colorize(" (override)", "cyan") if is_override else ""
    60→            print(f"    {rp}{suffix}")
    61→        print()
    62→
    63→    if overrides:

    65→    print(colorize("  Override: desloppify zone set <file> <zone>", "dim"))
    66→    print(colorize("  Clear:    desloppify zone clear <file>", "dim"))

    69→def _zone_set(args):

    73→    filepath = args.zone_path

     9→def cmd_resolve(args):
    10→    """Resolve finding(s) matching one or more patterns."""
    11→    from ..state import load_state, save_state, resolve_findings
    12→
    13→    if args.status == "wontfix" and not args.note:

    21→
    22→    all_resolved = []
    23→    for pattern in args.patterns:
    24→        resolved = resolve_findings(state, pattern, args.status, args.note)
    25→        all_resolved.extend(resolved)
    26→
    27→    if not all_resolved:

    29→        return
    30→
    31→    save_state(state, sp)
    32→

    36→    if len(all_resolved) > 20:

    38→

    43→                         if f["status"] in ("open", "wontfix", "fixed", "auto_resolved", "false_positive"))
    44→        wontfix_pct = round(wontfix_count / actionable * 100) if actionable else 0
    45→        print(colorize(f"\n  \u26a0 Wontfix debt is now {wontfix_count} findings ({wontfix_pct}% of actionable).", "yellow"))
    46→        print(colorize(f"    The strict score reflects this. Run `desloppify show \"*\" --status wontfix` to review.", "dim"))
    47→
    48→    new_obj = state.get("objective_score")

    59→              colorize(f"  (strict: {state.get('strict_score', 0):.1f}/100)", "dim"))

54→def load_config(path: Path | None = None) -> dict:
    55→    """Load config from disk, auto-migrating from state files if needed.
    56→
    57→    Fills missing keys with defaults. If no config.json exists, attempts
    58→    migration from state-*.json files.
    59→    """
    60→    p = path or CONFIG_FILE
    61→    if p.exists():
    62→        try:
    63→            config = json.loads(p.read_text())
    64→        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
    65→            config = {}
    66→    else:
    67→        # First run — try migrating from state files
    68→        config = _migrate_from_state_files(p)
    69→
    70→    # Fill missing keys with defaults
    71→    for key, schema in CONFIG_SCHEMA.items():
    72→        if key not in config:
    73→            config[key] = schema.default
    74→
    75→    return config
    76→
    77→
    78→def save_config(config: dict, path: Path | None = None) -> None:
    79→    """Save config to disk atomically."""
    80→    p = path or CONFIG_FILE
    81→    safe_write_text(p, json.dumps(config, indent=2) + "\n")

    13→    if args.status == "wontfix" and not args.note:

    21→
    22→    all_resolved = []
    23→    for pattern in args.patterns:
    24→        resolved = resolve_findings(state, pattern, args.status, args.note)
    25→        all_resolved.extend(resolved)

    27→    if not all_resolved:

    10→def cmd_zone(args):
    11→    """Handle zone subcommands: show, set, clear."""
    12→    action = getattr(args, "zone_action", None)
    13→    if action == "show":
    14→        _zone_show(args)
    15→    elif action == "set":
    16→        _zone_set(args)
    17→    elif action == "clear":
    18→        _zone_clear(args)

    20→        print(colorize("Usage: desloppify zone {show|set|clear}", "red"))

    22→
    23→def _zone_show(args):
    24→    """Show zone classifications for all scanned files."""
    25→    from ..state import load_state
    26→    from ._helpers import resolve_lang
    27→
    28→    sp = state_path(args)
    29→    load_state(sp)  # validate state file exists/loads
    30→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
    31→    if not lang or not lang.file_finder:
    32→        print(colorize("No language detected — run a scan first.", "red"))
    33→        return
    34→
    35→    path = Path(args.path)
    36→    overrides = args._config.get("zone_overrides", {})
    37→
    38→    from ..zones import FileZoneMap
    39→    files = lang.file_finder(path)
    40→    zone_map = FileZoneMap(files, lang.zone_rules, rel_fn=rel, overrides=overrides or None)
    41→
    42→    # Group files by zone
    43→    by_zone: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    44→    for f in sorted(files, key=lambda f: rel(f)):
    45→        zone = zone_map.get(f)
    46→        by_zone.setdefault(zone.value, []).append(f)
    47→
    48→    total = len(files)
    49→    print(colorize(f"\nZone classifications ({total} files)\n", "bold"))
    50→
    51→    for zone_val in ["production", "test", "config", "generated", "script", "vendor"]:
    52→        zone_files = by_zone.get(zone_val, [])
    53→        if not zone_files:
    54→            continue
    55→        print(colorize(f"  {zone_val} ({len(zone_files)} files)", "bold"))
    56→        for f in zone_files:
    57→            rp = rel(f)
    58→            is_override = rp in overrides
    59→            suffix = colorize(" (override)", "cyan") if is_override else ""
    60→            print(f"    {rp}{suffix}")
    61→        print()
    62→
    63→    if overrides:
    64→        print(colorize(f"  {len(overrides)} override(s) active", "dim"))
    65→    print(colorize("  Override: desloppify zone set <file> <zone>", "dim"))
    66→    print(colorize("  Clear:    desloppify zone clear <file>", "dim"))
    67→
    68→
    69→def _zone_set(args):
    70→    """Set a zone override for a file."""
    71→    from ..config import save_config
    72→
    73→    filepath = args.zone_path
    74→    zone_value = args.zone_value
    75→
    76→    # Validate zone value
    77→    valid_zones = {z.value for z in Zone}
    78→    if zone_value not in valid_zones:
    79→        print(colorize(f"Invalid zone: {zone_value}. Valid: {', '.join(sorted(valid_zones))}", "red"))
    80→        return
    81→
    82→    config = args._config
    83→    config.setdefault("zone_overrides", {})[filepath] = zone_value
    84→    save_config(config)
    85→    print(f"  Set {filepath} → {zone_value}")
    86→    print(colorize("  Run `desloppify scan` to apply.", "dim"))
    87→
    88→
    89→def _zone_clear(args):

    98→        save_config(args._config)
    99→        print(f"  Cleared override for {filepath}")
   100→        print(colorize("  Run `desloppify scan` to apply.", "dim"))

1→"""Language-agnostic dependency graph algorithms.
     2→
     3→The graph structure is: {resolved_path: {"imports": set, "importers": set, "import_count": int, "importer_count": int}}
     4→Language-specific modules build the graph; this module provides shared algorithms.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→
     9→from ..utils import rel, resolve_path, PROJECT_ROOT
    10→
    11→
    12→def finalize_graph(graph: dict) -> dict:
    13→    """Add counts to a raw graph (imports/importers sets only).
    14→
    15→    Also filters out nodes matching global --exclude patterns, and removes
    16→    references to excluded files from all import/importer sets.
    17→    """
    18→    from .. import utils as _utils_mod
    19→    _extra_exclusions = _utils_mod._extra_exclusions
    20→
    21→    # Remove excluded nodes and clean up references
    22→    # Use relative paths for exclusion matching to avoid false positives
    23→    # when an exclude pattern (e.g. "Wan2GP") matches the project root
    24→    # directory name (e.g. "Headless-Wan2GP").
    25→    if _extra_exclusions:
    26→        excluded_keys = set()
    27→        for k in graph:
    28→            try:
    29→                rel_k = str(Path(k).relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT))
    30→            except ValueError:
    31→                rel_k = k
    32→            if any(_utils_mod.matches_exclusion(rel_k, ex) for ex in _extra_exclusions):
    33→                excluded_keys.add(k)
    34→        for k in excluded_keys:
    35→            del graph[k]
    36→        # Clean import/importer sets of references to removed nodes
    37→        for v in graph.values():
    38→            v["imports"] = v["imports"] - excluded_keys
    39→            v["importers"] = v["importers"] - excluded_keys
    40→            if "deferred_imports" in v:
    41→                v["deferred_imports"] = v["deferred_imports"] - excluded_keys
    42→
    43→    for v in graph.values():
    44→        v["import_count"] = len(v["imports"])
    45→        v["importer_count"] = len(v["importers"])
    46→    return graph
    47→
    48→
    49→def detect_cycles(graph: dict, *, skip_deferred: bool = True) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    50→    """Find import cycles using Tarjan's strongly connected components (iterative).
    51→
    52→    When skip_deferred=True (default), deferred imports (inside functions) are
    53→    excluded from cycle detection — they can't cause circular import errors.
    54→
    55→    Returns (entries, total_files). Each entry: {"files": [abs_paths], "length": int}
    56→    """
    57→    index_counter = 0
    58→    scc_stack: list[str] = []
    59→    lowlinks: dict[str, int] = {}
    60→    index: dict[str, int] = {}
    61→    on_stack: dict[str, bool] = {}
    62→    sccs: list[list[str]] = []
    63→
    64→    def _get_edges(v: str) -> list[str]:
    65→        node = graph.get(v, {})
    66→        imports = node.get("imports", set())
    67→        if skip_deferred:
    68→            imports = imports - node.get("deferred_imports", set())
    69→        return [w for w in imports if w in graph]
    70→
    71→    for root in graph:
    72→        if root in index:
    73→            continue
    74→
    75→        # Iterative Tarjan's using an explicit call stack.
    76→        # Each frame is (node, edge_iterator, is_root_call).
    77→        # When we first visit a node we assign index/lowlink and push to SCC stack.
    78→        # When we finish iterating edges we check for SCC root.
    79→        call_stack: list[tuple[str, list[str], int]] = []
    80→        index[root] = lowlinks[root] = index_counter
    81→        index_counter += 1
    82→        scc_stack.append(root)
    83→        on_stack[root] = True
    84→        edges = _get_edges(root)
    85→        call_stack.append((root, edges, 0))
    86→
    87→        while call_stack:
    88→            v, edges, ei = call_stack[-1]
    89→
    90→            if ei < len(edges):
    91→                w = edges[ei]
    92→                call_stack[-1] = (v, edges, ei + 1)
    93→
    94→                if w not in index:
    95→                    # "Recurse" into w
    96→                    index[w] = lowlinks[w] = index_counter
    97→                    index_counter += 1
    98→                    scc_stack.append(w)
    99→                    on_stack[w] = True
   100→                    w_edges = _get_edges(w)
   101→                    call_stack.append((w, w_edges, 0))
   102→                elif on_stack.get(w, False):
   103→                    lowlinks[v] = min(lowlinks[v], index[w])
   104→            else:
   105→                # Done with all edges for v — check for SCC root
   106→                if lowlinks[v] == index[v]:
   107→                    component: list[str] = []
   108→                    while True:
   109→                        w = scc_stack.pop()
   110→                        on_stack[w] = False
   111→                        component.append(w)
   112→                        if w == v:
   113→                            break
   114→                    if len(component) > 1:
   115→                        component.sort()
   116→                        sccs.append(component)
   117→
   118→                call_stack.pop()
   119→                # Propagate lowlink to parent
   120→                if call_stack:
   121→                    parent = call_stack[-1][0]
   122→                    lowlinks[parent] = min(lowlinks[parent], lowlinks[v])
   123→
   124→    return [{"files": scc, "length": len(scc)} for scc in sorted(sccs, key=lambda s: -len(s))], len(graph)
   125→
   126→
   127→def get_coupling_score(filepath: str, graph: dict) -> dict:
   128→    """Get coupling metrics for a file."""
   129→    resolved = resolve_path(filepath)
   130→    entry = graph.get(resolved, {"imports": set(), "importers": set(), "import_count": 0, "importer_count": 0})
   131→    fan_in = entry["importer_count"]
   132→    fan_out = entry["import_count"]
   133→    instability = fan_out / (fan_in + fan_out) if (fan_in + fan_out) > 0 else 0
   134→    return {
   135→        "fan_in": fan_in,
   136→        "fan_out": fan_out,
   137→        "instability": round(instability, 2),
   138→        "importers": [rel(p) for p in sorted(entry["importers"])],
   139→        "imports": [rel(p) for p in sorted(entry["imports"])],
   140→    }
   141→

1→"""DictKeyVisitor — AST visitor tracking dict key writes/reads per scope."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import ast
     6→
     7→from .dict_keys import TrackedDict, _CONFIG_NAMES, _get_name, _get_str_key, _BULK_READ_METHODS, _levenshtein, _is_singular_plural
     8→
     9→
    10→class DictKeyVisitor(ast.NodeVisitor):
    11→    """Walk a module AST, tracking dict key writes/reads per function scope."""
    12→
    13→    def __init__(self, filepath: str):
    14→        self.filepath = filepath
    15→        self._scopes: list[dict[str, TrackedDict]] = []
    16→        self._class_dicts: dict[str, TrackedDict] = {}  # self.x dicts
    17→        self._in_init_or_setup = False
    18→        self._findings: list[dict] = []
    19→        self._dict_literals: list[dict] = []  # for schema drift
    20→
    21→    def _current_scope(self) -> dict[str, TrackedDict]:
    22→        return self._scopes[-1] if self._scopes else {}
    23→
    24→    def _track(self, name: str, line: int, *, locally_created: bool,
    25→               initial_keys: list[str] | None = None) -> TrackedDict:
    26→        scope = self._current_scope()
    27→        td = TrackedDict(name=name, created_line=line, locally_created=locally_created)
    28→        if initial_keys:
    29→            for k in initial_keys:
    30→                td.writes[k].append(line)
    31→        scope[name] = td
    32→        return td
    33→
    34→    def _get_tracked(self, name: str) -> TrackedDict | None:
    35→        # Check current scope first, then class scope for self.x
    36→        for scope in reversed(self._scopes):
    37→            if name in scope:
    38→                return scope[name]
    39→        if name.startswith("self.") and name in self._class_dicts:
    40→            return self._class_dicts[name]
    41→        return None
    42→
    43→    def _mark_returned_or_passed(self, node: ast.expr):
    44→        """Mark a dict as returned or passed to a function."""
    45→        # Handle tuples: return (a, b) or func(a, b)
    46→        if isinstance(node, ast.Tuple):
    47→            for elt in node.elts:
    48→                self._mark_returned_or_passed(elt)
    49→            return
    50→        name = _get_name(node)
    51→        if name:
    52→            td = self._get_tracked(name)
    53→            if td:
    54→                td.returned_or_passed = True
    55→
    56→    # -- Scope management --
    57→
    58→    def visit_FunctionDef(self, node: ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
    59→        prev_init = self._in_init_or_setup
    60→        self._in_init_or_setup = node.name in ("__init__", "setUp", "setup")
    61→        self._scopes.append({})
    62→        self.generic_visit(node)
    63→        scope = self._scopes.pop()
    64→        self._analyze_scope(scope, node.name)
    65→        self._in_init_or_setup = prev_init
    66→
    67→    visit_AsyncFunctionDef = visit_FunctionDef
    68→
    69→    def visit_ClassDef(self, node: ast.ClassDef):
    70→        prev_class_dicts = self._class_dicts
    71→        self._class_dicts = {}
    72→        self.generic_visit(node)
    73→        self._analyze_scope(self._class_dicts, f"class {node.name}", is_class=True)
    74→        self._class_dicts = prev_class_dicts
    75→
    76→    # -- Dict creation --
    77→
    78→    def visit_Assign(self, node: ast.Assign):
    79→        if len(node.targets) == 1:
    80→            target = node.targets[0]
    81→            name = _get_name(target)
    82→            if name:
    83→                self._check_dict_creation(name, node.value, node.lineno)
    84→        # Also check for subscript writes: d["key"] = val
    85→        for target in node.targets:
    86→            self._check_subscript_write(target, node.lineno)
    87→        self.generic_visit(node)
    88→
    89→    def visit_AugAssign(self, node: ast.AugAssign):
    90→        # AugAssign (d["k"] += v) is both a read AND a write
    91→        if isinstance(node.target, ast.Subscript):
    92→            name = _get_name(node.target.value)
    93→            if name:
    94→                td = self._get_tracked(name)
    95→                if td:
    96→                    key = _get_str_key(node.target.slice)
    97→                    if key:
    98→                        td.reads[key].append(node.lineno)
    99→                    else:
   100→                        td.has_dynamic_key = True
   101→        self._check_subscript_write(node.target, node.lineno)
   102→        self.generic_visit(node)
   103→
   104→    def _check_dict_creation(self, name: str, value: ast.expr, line: int):
   105→        """Detect d = {}, d = dict(), d = {"k": v, ...}."""
   106→        initial_keys: list[str] = []
   107→        is_creation = False
   108→
   109→        if isinstance(value, ast.Dict):
   110→            is_creation = True
   111→            for k in value.keys:
   112→                sk = _get_str_key(k) if k else None
   113→                if sk:
   114→                    initial_keys.append(sk)
   115→            # Collect dict literal for schema drift
   116→            if all(isinstance(k, ast.Constant) and isinstance(k.value, str)
   117→                   for k in value.keys if k is not None) and len(value.keys) >= 3:
   118→                keys = [k.value for k in value.keys if isinstance(k, ast.Constant)]
   119→                self._dict_literals.append({
   120→                    "file": self.filepath, "line": line,
   121→                    "keys": frozenset(keys),
   122→                })
   123→        elif (isinstance(value, ast.Call) and isinstance(value.func, ast.Name)
   124→              and value.func.id == "dict"):
   125→            is_creation = True
   126→            for kw in value.keywords:
   127→                if kw.arg:
   128→                    initial_keys.append(kw.arg)
   129→
   130→        if is_creation:
   131→            td = self._track(name, line, locally_created=True,
   132→                             initial_keys=initial_keys)
   133→            # Store as class dict if it's self.x
   134→            if name.startswith("self.") and self._in_init_or_setup:
   135→                self._class_dicts[name] = td
   136→
   137→    def _check_subscript_write(self, target: ast.expr, line: int):
   138→        """Handle d["key"] = val or d["key"] += val."""
   139→        if not isinstance(target, ast.Subscript):
   140→            return
   141→        name = _get_name(target.value)
   142→        if not name:
   143→            return
   144→        key = _get_str_key(target.slice)
   145→        td = self._get_tracked(name)
   146→        if td is None:
   147→            return
   148→        if key:
   149→            td.writes[key].append(line)
   150→        else:
   151→            td.has_dynamic_key = True
   152→
   153→    # -- Dict reads --
   154→
   155→    def visit_Subscript(self, node: ast.Subscript):
   156→        if isinstance(node.ctx, ast.Load):
   157→            name = _get_name(node.value)
   158→            if name:
   159→                td = self._get_tracked(name)
   160→                if td:
   161→                    key = _get_str_key(node.slice)
   162→                    if key:
   163→                        td.reads[key].append(node.lineno)
   164→                    else:
   165→                        td.has_dynamic_key = True
   166→        self.generic_visit(node)
   167→
   168→    def visit_Delete(self, node: ast.Delete):
   169→        for target in node.targets:
   170→            if isinstance(target, ast.Subscript):
   171→                name = _get_name(target.value)
   172→                if name:
   173→                    td = self._get_tracked(name)
   174→                    if td:
   175→                        key = _get_str_key(target.slice)
   176→                        if key:
   177→                            td.reads[key].append(target.lineno)
   178→                        else:
   179→                            td.has_dynamic_key = True
   180→        self.generic_visit(node)
   181→
   182→    def visit_Call(self, node: ast.Call):
   183→        # Check method calls on tracked dicts: d.get("key"), d.update({...}), etc.
   184→        if isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute):
   185→            name = _get_name(node.func.value)
   186→            method = node.func.attr
   187→            if name:
   188→                td = self._get_tracked(name)
   189→                if td:
   190→                    if method in ("get", "pop", "__getitem__", "__contains__"):
   191→                        if node.args:
   192→                            key = _get_str_key(node.args[0])
   193→                            if key:
   194→                                td.reads[key].append(node.lineno)
   195→                            else:
   196→                                td.has_dynamic_key = True
   197→                    elif method == "setdefault":
   198→                        if node.args:
   199→                            key = _get_str_key(node.args[0])
   200→                            if key:
   201→                                td.reads[key].append(node.lineno)
   202→                                td.writes[key].append(node.lineno)
   203→                            else:
   204→                                td.has_dynamic_key = True
   205→                    elif method == "update":
   206→                        # d.update({"k": v}) or d.update(k=v)
   207→                        if node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Dict):
   208→                            for k in node.args[0].keys:
   209→                                sk = _get_str_key(k) if k else None
   210→                                if sk:
   211→                                    td.writes[sk].append(node.lineno)
   212→                                elif k is None:
   213→                                    td.has_dynamic_key = True
   214→                        for kw in node.keywords:
   215→                            if kw.arg:
   216→                                td.writes[kw.arg].append(node.lineno)
   217→                            else:
   218→                                td.has_dynamic_key = True  # **kwargs
   219→                    elif method in _BULK_READ_METHODS:
   220→                        td.bulk_read = True
   221→
   222→        # Check if a tracked dict is passed as argument (mark as escaped)
   223→        for arg in node.args:
   224→            self._mark_returned_or_passed(arg)
   225→        for kw in node.keywords:
   226→            if kw.arg is None:  # **d
   227→                name = _get_name(kw.value)
   228→                if name:
   229→                    td = self._get_tracked(name)
   230→                    if td:
   231→                        td.has_star_unpack = True
   232→            else:
   233→                self._mark_returned_or_passed(kw.value)
   234→
   235→        self.generic_visit(node)
   236→
   237→    def visit_Return(self, node: ast.Return):
   238→        if node.value:
   239→            self._mark_returned_or_passed(node.value)
   240→            # Also handle return {"k": v, ...} — not a tracked dict, but
   241→            # handle return d where d is tracked
   242→        self.generic_visit(node)
   243→
   244→    def visit_Yield(self, node: ast.Yield):
   245→        if node.value:
   246→            self._mark_returned_or_passed(node.value)
   247→        self.generic_visit(node)
   248→
   249→    def visit_YieldFrom(self, node: ast.YieldFrom):
   250→        if node.value:
   251→            self._mark_returned_or_passed(node.value)
   252→        self.generic_visit(node)

   254→    def visit_Compare(self, node: ast.Compare):
   255→        """Handle "key" in d."""
   256→        for i, op in enumerate(node.ops):
   257→            if isinstance(op, (ast.In, ast.NotIn)):
   258→                comparator = node.comparators[i]
   259→                name = _get_name(comparator)
   260→                if name:
   261→                    td = self._get_tracked(name)
   262→                    if td:
   263→                        # The left side of `in` for the first op is node.left
   264→                        left = node.left if i == 0 else node.comparators[i - 1]
   265→                        key = _get_str_key(left)
   266→                        if key:
   267→                            td.reads[key].append(node.lineno)
   268→        self.generic_visit(node)

   270→    def visit_For(self, node: ast.For):
   271→        """Handle `for x in d` — bulk read."""
   272→        name = _get_name(node.iter)
   273→        if name:
   274→            td = self._get_tracked(name)
   275→            if td:
   276→                td.bulk_read = True
   277→        self.generic_visit(node)

   280→        """Handle {**d} or func(*d)."""

   282→        if name:
   283→            td = self._get_tracked(name)
   284→            if td:
   285→                td.has_star_unpack = True
   286→        self.generic_visit(node)

   288→    # -- Dict literal collection (standalone, non-assigned) --
   289→
   290→    def visit_Dict(self, node: ast.Dict):
   291→        """Collect dict literals for schema drift analysis."""
   292→        if (all(isinstance(k, ast.Constant) and isinstance(k.value, str)
   293→                for k in node.keys if k is not None)
   294→                and len(node.keys) >= 3
   295→                and all(k is not None for k in node.keys)):
   296→            keys = frozenset(k.value for k in node.keys if isinstance(k, ast.Constant))
   297→            self._dict_literals.append({
   298→                "file": self.filepath, "line": node.lineno,
   299→                "keys": keys,
   300→            })
   301→        self.generic_visit(node)

   303→    # -- Scope analysis --
   304→
   305→    def _analyze_scope(self, scope: dict[str, TrackedDict], func_name: str,
   306→                       *, is_class: bool = False):
   307→        """Analyze a completed scope for dict key issues."""
   308→        for td in scope.values():
   309→            if not td.locally_created:
   310→                continue
   311→
   312→            # Determine if dead-write warnings should be suppressed
   313→            suppress_dead = (
   314→                td.returned_or_passed
   315→                or td.has_dynamic_key
   316→                or td.has_star_unpack
   317→                or td.bulk_read
   318→                or any(td.name.lower().endswith(n) or td.name.lower() == n
   319→                       for n in _CONFIG_NAMES)
   320→                or (not is_class and func_name in ("__init__", "setUp", "setup"))
   321→                or sum(len(v) for v in td.writes.values()) < 3
   322→            )
   323→
   324→            written_keys = set(td.writes.keys())
   325→            read_keys = set(td.reads.keys())
   326→
   327→            # Dead writes: written but never read
   328→            dead_keys = written_keys - read_keys
   329→            if not suppress_dead:
   330→                for key in sorted(dead_keys):
   331→                    lines = td.writes[key]
   332→                    self._findings.append({
   333→                        "file": self.filepath, "kind": "dead_write",
   334→                        "variable": td.name, "key": key,
   335→                        "line": lines[0], "func": func_name,
   336→                        "tier": 3, "confidence": "medium",
   337→                        "summary": (f'Dict key "{key}" written to `{td.name}` '
   338→                                    f'at line {lines[0]} but never read'),
   339→                        "detail": f"in {func_name}()",
   340→                    })
   341→
   342→            # Phantom reads: read but never written (on locally-created dict)
   343→            phantom_keys = read_keys - written_keys
   344→            for key in sorted(phantom_keys):
   345→                lines = td.reads[key]
   346→                self._findings.append({
   347→                    "file": self.filepath, "kind": "phantom_read",
   348→                    "variable": td.name, "key": key,
   349→                    "line": lines[0], "func": func_name,
   350→                    "tier": 2, "confidence": "high",
   351→                    "summary": (f'Dict key "{key}" read at line {lines[0]} '
   352→                                f'but never written to `{td.name}`'),
   353→                    "detail": (f"Created at line {td.created_line} in "
   354→                               f"{func_name}() — will raise KeyError or "
   355→                               f"return None via .get()"),
   356→                })
   357→
   358→            # Near-miss: dead write key ≈ phantom read key
   359→            for dk in sorted(dead_keys):
   360→                for pk in sorted(phantom_keys):
   361→                    dist = _levenshtein(dk, pk)
   362→                    is_sp = _is_singular_plural(dk, pk)
   363→                    if dist <= 2 or is_sp:
   364→                        write_line = td.writes[dk][0]
   365→                        read_line = td.reads[pk][0]
   366→                        self._findings.append({
   367→                            "file": self.filepath, "kind": "near_miss",
   368→                            "variable": td.name, "key": f"{dk}~{pk}",
   369→                            "line": write_line, "func": func_name,
   370→                            "tier": 2, "confidence": "high",
   371→                            "summary": (f'Possible key typo: "{dk}" vs "{pk}" '
   372→                                        f'on dict `{td.name}` in {func_name}()'),
   373→                            "detail": (f'Written: "{dk}" at line {write_line}, '
   374→                                       f'Read: "{pk}" at line {read_line} '
   375→                                       f'— edit distance {dist}'),
   376→                        })
   377→
   378→            # Overwritten keys: same key assigned twice with no read between
   379→            for key, write_lines in td.writes.items():
   380→                if len(write_lines) < 2:
   381→                    continue
   382→                read_lines = td.reads.get(key, [])
   383→                for i in range(len(write_lines) - 1):
   384→                    w1, w2 = write_lines[i], write_lines[i + 1]
   385→                    # Check if any read of this key occurs between w1 and w2
   386→                    has_read_between = any(w1 < r <= w2 for r in read_lines)
   387→                    if not has_read_between:
   388→                        self._findings.append({
   389→                            "file": self.filepath, "kind": "overwritten_key",
   390→                            "variable": td.name, "key": key,
   391→                            "line": w2, "func": func_name,
   392→                            "tier": 3, "confidence": "medium",
   393→                            "summary": (f'Dict key "{key}" overwritten on `{td.name}` '
   394→                                        f'at line {w2} (previously set at line {w1}, '
   395→                                        f'never read between)'),
   396→                            "detail": f"in {func_name}()",
   397→                        })
   398→

    12→def scan_code(text: str, start: int = 0, end: int | None = None):
    13→    """Yield (index, char, in_string) tuples, handling escapes correctly.
    14→

    16→    Tracks single-quoted, double-quoted, and template literal strings.
    17→    Correct for \\\\\" (escaped backslash before quote) where prev_ch pattern fails.
    18→    """
    19→    i = start

    21→    in_str = None
    22→    while i < limit:
    23→        ch = text[i]
    24→        if in_str:

    27→                i += 1

    36→                in_str = ch
    37→                yield (i, ch, True)
    38→            else:

    40→        i += 1

   224→def _detect_dead_useeffects(filepath: str, lines: list[str],

   247→                    paren_depth += 1
   248→                elif ch == ")":
   249→                    paren_depth -= 1
   250→                    if paren_depth <= 0:
   251→                        end = j
   252→                        break
   253→                elif ch == "{":
   254→                    brace_depth += 1
   255→                elif ch == "}":
   256→                    brace_depth -= 1

   260→        if end is None:

   262→

   268→        if brace_pos == -1:

   273→        for ci, ch, in_s in scan_code(text, brace_pos):
   274→            if in_s:

   276→            if ch == "{":
   277→                depth += 1
   278→            elif ch == "}":
   279→                depth -= 1
   280→                if depth == 0:
   281→                    body_end = ci
   282→                    break

   284→        if body_end is None:

   287→        body = text[brace_pos + 1:body_end]

   302→    string-escape awareness to extract the catch body (up to 500 chars).
   303→    Strip comments, split into statements, and check if every statement
   304→    is a console.error/warn/log call.
   305→    """
   306→    catch_re = re.compile(r"catch\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{")
   307→    for m in catch_re.finditer(content):
   308→        brace_start = m.end() - 1
   309→        depth = 0
   310→        body_end = None
   311→        for ci, ch, in_s in scan_code(content, brace_start, min(brace_start + 500, len(content))):
   312→            if in_s:
   313→                continue
   314→            if ch == "{":
   315→                depth += 1
   316→            elif ch == "}":
   317→                depth -= 1
   318→                if depth == 0:
   319→                    body_end = ci
   320→                    break
   321→
   322→        if body_end is None:
   323→            continue
   324→
   325→        body = content[brace_start + 1:body_end]
   326→        body_clean = _strip_ts_comments(body).strip()

   328→        if not body_clean:
   329→            continue  # empty catch — caught by empty_catch detector
   330→
   331→        statements = [s.strip().rstrip(";") for s in re.split(r"[;\n]", body_clean) if s.strip()]
   332→        if not statements:
   333→            continue

   335→        all_console = all(
   336→            re.match(r"console\.(error|warn|log)\s*\(", stmt)
   337→            for stmt in statements
   338→        )
   339→        if all_console:
   340→            line_no = content[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1
   341→            smell_counts["swallowed_error"].append({
   342→                "file": filepath,
   343→                "line": line_no,
   344→                "content": lines[line_no - 1].strip()[:100] if line_no <= len(lines) else "",
   345→            })

   347→
   348→def _track_brace_body(lines: list[str], start_line: int, *, max_scan: int = 2000) -> int | None:
   349→    """Find the closing brace that matches the first opening brace from start_line.
   350→
   351→    Tracks brace depth with string-literal awareness (', ", `).
   352→    Returns the line index of the closing brace, or None if not found.
   353→    """
   354→    depth = 0
   355→    found_open = False
   356→    for j in range(start_line, min(start_line + max_scan, len(lines))):
   357→        for _, ch, in_s in scan_code(lines[j]):
   358→            if in_s:
   359→                continue
   360→            if ch == "{":
   361→                depth += 1
   362→                found_open = True
   363→            elif ch == "}":
   364→                depth -= 1
   365→                if found_open and depth == 0:
   366→                    return j
   367→    return None

1→"""Mixed concerns detection (UI + data fetching + transforms in one file)."""
     2→
     3→import json
     4→import re
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from ....utils import PROJECT_ROOT, c, find_tsx_files, print_table, rel
     8→
     9→
    10→def detect_mixed_concerns(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    11→    """Find files that mix UI rendering with data fetching, state management, and business logic.
    12→
    13→    Heuristic: a .tsx file that has both JSX returns AND direct API/supabase calls
    14→    or both UI components AND heavy data transformation.
    15→
    16→    Returns (entries, total_files_checked).
    17→    """
    18→    files = find_tsx_files(path)
    19→    entries = []
    20→    for filepath in files:
    21→        try:
    22→            p = Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / filepath
    23→            content = p.read_text()
    24→            loc = len(content.splitlines())
    25→            if loc < 100:
    26→                continue
    27→
    28→            concerns = []
    29→
    30→            # UI rendering
    31→            has_jsx = bool(re.search(r"return\s*\(?\s*<", content))
    32→            if has_jsx:
    33→                concerns.append("jsx_rendering")
    34→
    35→            # Data fetching
    36→            has_fetch = bool(re.search(r"useQuery|useMutation|supabase\.|fetch\(|axios", content))
    37→            if has_fetch:
    38→                concerns.append("data_fetching")
    39→
    40→            # Direct supabase calls (should be in hooks/services)
    41→            has_supabase = bool(re.search(r"supabase\.\w+\.\w+\.\w+", content))
    42→            if has_supabase:
    43→                concerns.append("direct_supabase")
    44→
    45→            # Heavy data transformation
    46→            transform_patterns = len(re.findall(r"\.(map|filter|reduce|sort|flatMap)\s*\(", content))
    47→            if transform_patterns >= 3:
    48→                concerns.append(f"data_transforms({transform_patterns})")
    49→
    50→            # Event handler definitions (>5 = probably doing too much)
    51→            handler_count = len(re.findall(r"(?:const|function)\s+handle\w+", content))
    52→            if handler_count >= 5:
    53→                concerns.append(f"handlers({handler_count})")
    54→
    55→            # Flag if 3+ concern types in one file
    56→            if len(concerns) >= 3:
    57→                entries.append({
    58→                    "file": filepath, "loc": loc,
    59→                    "concerns": concerns,
    60→                    "concern_count": len(concerns),
    61→                })
    62→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
    63→            continue
    64→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["concern_count"]), len(files)
    65→
    66→
    67→def cmd_concerns(args):
    68→    entries, _ = detect_mixed_concerns(Path(args.path))
    69→    if args.json:
    70→        print(json.dumps({"count": len(entries), "entries": entries}, indent=2))
    71→        return
    72→    if not entries:
    73→        print(c("No mixed-concern files found.", "green"))
    74→        return
    75→    print(c(f"\nMixed concerns: {len(entries)} files\n", "bold"))
    76→    rows = []
    77→    for e in entries[:args.top]:
    78→        rows.append([rel(e["file"]), str(e["loc"]), ", ".join(e["concerns"])])
    79→    print_table(["File", "LOC", "Concerns"], rows, [55, 5, 50])
    80→

1→"""Stale @deprecated shim detection."""
     2→
     3→import json
     4→import re
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from ....utils import (PROJECT_ROOT, SRC_PATH, c, grep_count_files, grep_files,
     8→                       print_table, rel, resolve_path)
     9→
    10→
    11→def detect_deprecated(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    12→    from ....utils import find_ts_files
    13→    ts_files = find_ts_files(path)
    14→    hits = grep_files(r"@deprecated", ts_files)
    15→
    16→    entries = []
    17→    seen_symbols = set()  # Deduplicate by file+symbol
    18→    for filepath, lineno, content in hits:
    19→        symbol, kind = _extract_deprecated_symbol(filepath, lineno, content)
    20→        if not symbol:
    21→            continue
    22→        # Deduplicate (same symbol in same file, e.g., multiple @deprecated on interface props)
    23→        key = (filepath, symbol)
    24→        if key in seen_symbols:
    25→            continue
    26→        seen_symbols.add(key)
    27→        importers = _count_importers(symbol, filepath) if kind == "top-level" else -1
    28→        entries.append({
    29→            "file": filepath,
    30→            "line": lineno,
    31→            "symbol": symbol,
    32→            "kind": kind,
    33→            "importers": importers,
    34→        })
    35→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: e["importers"]), len(entries)
    36→
    37→
    38→def _extract_deprecated_symbol(filepath: str, lineno: int, content: str) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    39→    """Extract the deprecated symbol name and whether it's a top-level or inline deprecation.
    40→
    41→    Returns (symbol_name, kind) where kind is "top-level" or "property".
    42→    """
    43→    try:
    44→        p = Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / filepath
    45→        lines = p.read_text().splitlines()
    46→        content_stripped = content.strip()
    47→
    48→        # Case 1: Inline @deprecated on a property/field
    49→        # e.g., `/** @deprecated Use X instead */ fieldName?: Type;`
    50→        # or `/** @deprecated */ export const oldThing = ...`
    51→        if "/**" in content_stripped and "*/" in content_stripped:
    52→            # This is a single-line JSDoc. Check what follows on the same or next line
    53→            after_jsdoc = content_stripped.split("*/", 1)[1].strip() if "*/" in content_stripped else ""
    54→            if after_jsdoc:
    55→                # Property on same line: `/** @deprecated */ someField?: string;`
    56→                m = re.match(r"(\w+)\s*[?:=]", after_jsdoc)
    57→                if m:
    58→                    return m.group(1), "property"
    59→                # Declaration on same line: `/** @deprecated */ export const foo`
    60→                m = re.match(r"(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var|function|class|type|interface|enum)\s+(\w+)", after_jsdoc)
    61→                if m:
    62→                    return m.group(1), "top-level"
    63→
    64→        # Case 2: @deprecated inside a multi-line JSDoc block — check if it's on a property
    65→        # We need to look ahead to find what this annotates
    66→        for offset in range(1, 8):
    67→            idx = lineno - 1 + offset
    68→            if idx >= len(lines):
    69→                break
    70→            src = lines[idx].strip()
    71→            # Skip empty lines, comment continuations, closing comment
    72→            if not src or src.startswith("*") or src.startswith("//"):
    73→                if src == "*/":
    74→                    continue
    75→                if src.startswith("*"):
    76→                    continue
    77→                continue
    78→            # Top-level declaration
    79→            m = re.match(
    80→                r"(?:export\s+)?(?:declare\s+)?(?:const|let|var|function|class|type|interface|enum)\s+(\w+)",
    81→                src,
    82→            )
    83→            if m:
    84→                return m.group(1), "top-level"
    85→            # Property/field: `fieldName?: Type;` or `fieldName: Type;`
    86→            m = re.match(r"(\w+)\s*[?:]", src)
    87→            if m:
    88→                return m.group(1), "property"
    89→            break
    90→
    91→        # Case 3: @deprecated as inline comment on same line
    92→        # e.g., `shotImageEntryId?: string; // @deprecated`
    93→        # Check the current line for a preceding field name
    94→        if "//" in content_stripped or "*" in content_stripped:
    95→            # Look at the same line before the @deprecated
    96→            line_before = content_stripped.split("@deprecated")[0].strip().rstrip("/*").rstrip("*").strip()
    97→            m = re.search(r"(\w+)\s*[?:]", line_before)
    98→            if m:
    99→                return m.group(1), "property"
   100→
   101→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
   102→        pass
   103→    return None, "unknown"
   104→
   105→
   106→def _count_importers(name: str, declaring_file: str) -> int:
   107→    if not name:
   108→        return -1
   109→    from ....utils import find_ts_files
   110→    ts_files = find_ts_files(SRC_PATH)
   111→    matching = grep_count_files(name, ts_files, word_boundary=True)
   112→    declaring_resolved = resolve_path(declaring_file)
   113→    count = 0
   114→    for match_file in matching:
   115→        if resolve_path(match_file) != declaring_resolved:
   116→            count += 1
   117→    return count
   118→
   119→
   120→def cmd_deprecated(args):
   121→    entries, _ = detect_deprecated(Path(args.path))
   122→    if args.json:
   123→        print(json.dumps({"count": len(entries), "entries": entries}, indent=2))
   124→        return
   125→
   126→    if not entries:
   127→        print(c("No @deprecated annotations found.", "green"))
   128→        return
   129→
   130→    # Separate top-level and property deprecations
   131→    top_level = [e for e in entries if e["kind"] == "top-level"]
   132→    properties = [e for e in entries if e["kind"] == "property"]
   133→
   134→    print(c(f"\nDeprecated symbols: {len(entries)} ({len(top_level)} top-level, {len(properties)} properties)\n", "bold"))
   135→
   136→    if top_level:
   137→        print(c("Top-level (importable):", "cyan"))
   138→        rows = []

   140→            imp = str(e["importers"]) if e["importers"] >= 0 else "?"
   141→            status = c("safe to remove", "green") if e["importers"] == 0 else f"{imp} importers"
   142→            rows.append([e["symbol"], rel(e["file"]), status])

   149→        for e in properties[: args.top]:
   150→            rows.append([e["symbol"], rel(e["file"]), f"line {e['line']}"])
   151→        print_table(["Property", "File", "Line"], rows, [30, 55, 10])
